articles.excerpt: 📞 No more spam surprises! India will roll out a verified caller ID system — CNAP (Calling Name Presentation) — by March 2026. Every call will show the caller’s real KYC-verified name, not just the number.

body.html:
📞 No more spam surprises!
India will roll out a verified caller ID system — CNAP (Calling Name Presentation) — by March 2026. Every call will show the caller’s real KYC-verified name, not just the number.

Built into telecom networks (Airtel, Jio, Vi), CNAP will use government-verified data — not apps like Truecaller — to fight fraud and spam.

articles.title: High-Speed Horror in Pune: Two Killed as Car Crashes Near Bund Garden Metro Station! #viralvideo
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Pune, November 2 — Two people were killed and one seriously injured in a horrific car crash near Bund Garden Metro Station early Saturday morning around 5:10 a.m. Police said a black Volkswagen Polo with three occupants lost control and crashed violently near the station.

body.html:
Pune, November 2 — Two people were killed and one seriously injured in a horrific car crash near Bund Garden Metro Station early Saturday morning around 5:10 a.m.

Police said a black Volkswagen Polo with three occupants lost control and crashed violently near the station. The front of the car was completely mangled due to the impact.

Emergency teams rushed to the scene, but two occupants were declared dead on the spot. The third was taken to a nearby hospital in critical condition.

Preliminary investigations suggest overspeeding as the likely cause. CCTV footage of the incident has gone viral, with one user commenting, “It looks like they were trying to drift.”

articles.title: Heroic Rescue on Tracks! RPF Constable Saves Woman From Being Crushed Under Moving Train
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A major tragedy was narrowly averted at a railway station in Tamil Nadu when a woman attempting to board a moving train slipped and nearly fell into the gap between the platform and the train.

body.html:
A major tragedy was narrowly averted at a railway station in Tamil Nadu when a woman attempting to board a moving train slipped and nearly fell into the gap between the platform and the train. Thanks to the quick reflexes of a Railway Protection Force (RPF) officer, the woman’s life was saved in the nick of time.

The dramatic incident, captured on CCTV footage now going viral, shows the woman trying to hop onto the Erode–Chennai Yercaud Express (Train No. 22650) as it was leaving the station. Within seconds, she loses her balance and almost slips beneath the train.

Acting instantly, RPF Head Constable Sri Jagadeesan, who was on patrol at Erode Junction, rushed to the spot and pulled her to safety, preventing what could have been a horrifying accident.

The Southern Railway’s official X handle shared the video with the caption:

“Operation Jeevan Raksha – Commendable Act. Alertness saves lives! On 27.10.2025, Sri Jagadeesan, RPF Head Constable, Karur/SR, Erode Junction, promptly rescued a lady passenger who slipped while attempting to board Train No. 22650 Erode - Chennai Yercaud Express. His timely action saved a precious life. Kudos to RPF Constable Sri. Jagadeesan for his exemplary presence of mind and dedication!”

The video has since garnered over 32,000 views, with social media users praising the constable’s bravery and quick thinking. Many also urged railway authorities to reward Jagadeesan for his heroic act and to improve safety measures to prevent such incidents in the future.

articles.title: Two-Storey House Crumbles Like a Pack of Cards — Negligence or Fate?
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A major incident was reported from Shahpur area of Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh, where a two-storey house suddenly collapsed near the Guddaya (Godhiya) drain on Friday, sparking panic among locals. A LIVE video of the collapse is now going viral across social media platforms.

body.html:
A major incident was reported from Shahpur area of Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh, where a two-storey house suddenly collapsed near the Guddaya (Godhiya) drain on Friday, sparking panic among locals. A LIVE video of the collapse is now going viral across social media platforms.

According to sources, no casualties have been reported so far. Police and local administration teams immediately reached the spot and began rescue and debris removal operations. An investigation is underway to determine the cause of the collapse.

Locals recalled that about 10 days ago, cracks had appeared in three nearby houses during excavation work. Residents had vacated their homes as a precaution, which likely prevented a major tragedy. The incident has now raised serious questions about administrative negligence, with fingers being pointed at the revenue officer allegedly responsible for the excavation work.

For many residents, watching their home crumble was heartbreaking. “How many dreams and years of hard work went into building that house — and in just seconds, it turned to dust,” said one local with moist eyes.

articles.title: Caught Red-Handed! UP Police Sub-Inspector Nabbed Taking ₹2 Lakh Bribe Inside Station
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: In a major embarrassment for the Uttar Pradesh Police, Sub-Inspector Dhananjay Singh was arrested by the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) in Lucknow after being caught red-handed accepting a bribe of ₹2 lakh.

body.html:
In a major embarrassment for the Uttar Pradesh Police, Sub-Inspector Dhananjay Singh was arrested by the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) in Lucknow after being caught red-handed accepting a bribe of ₹2 lakh. The incident, which took place on October 29, 2025, at the Paper Mill Colony police outpost, was captured in a viral video that has since sparked outrage.

According to reports, Singh had demanded money from Prateek Gupta, a local coaching centre owner, in exchange for removing his name from a gang-rape case FIR filed on September 9, 2025, at the Mahanagar police station. Initially, Singh had allegedly asked for ₹50 lakh, but later settled for ₹2 lakh after negotiations.

Gupta reported the matter to the Anti-Corruption Organisation (ACO), which laid a trap. During the sting operation, Singh was seen in the viral clip calmly accepting bundles of ₹500 notes, which he then hid inside a file. Moments later, ACB officials entered the outpost and arrested him on the spot. The marked currency was recovered immediately.

Singh has been booked under the Prevention of Corruption Act, and a detailed investigation is underway to determine if other officers were involved. The Lucknow Police Commissionerate has also initiated departmental action against him.

articles.title: Villagers Force Child Marriage After Catching Teen Couple in Forest — SP Leader Seen Blessing the
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Fatehpur, Uttar Pradesh – A shocking case of child marriage has surfaced after villagers caught a teenage couple meeting secretly in a forest. The incident took place in Bhagwantpur village under the Radhanagar police station area.

body.html:
Fatehpur, Uttar Pradesh – A shocking case of child marriage has surfaced after villagers caught a teenage couple meeting secretly in a forest. The incident took place in Bhagwantpur village under the Radhanagar police station area.

After catching the duo, villagers informed the girl’s family and arranged their marriage at a temple outside the village. Shockingly, a Samajwadi Party leader was present and even blessed the newlyweds as the boy applied vermillion to the girl’s forehead and exchanged garlands. The video of the ceremony went viral on social media.

Following the uproar, the district administration and Child Line team intervened. Police detained both minors and presented them before the Child Welfare Committee. On court orders, the girl was sent to a One Stop Center, while the boy was placed at the Child Line Center.

Officials are now identifying those responsible for conducting the illegal marriage. Authorities have confirmed that strict action will be taken under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006.
